'''Abe Ariyo''' (安倍 有世) was a noble and {{ill|Onmyōji|en|Onmyōji|qid=Q2274163|lt=Onmyōji}} who lived during the {{ill|Northern and Southern Courts period (disambiguation)|en|Northern and Southern Courts period (disambiguation)|qid=Q8140349|lt=Nanboku-chō period}} and early {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}. He was the 14th-generation descendant of {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|Abe no Seimei|qid=Q1150151|lt=Abe no Seimei}}. Ariyo became the first Onmyōji to rise to the Rank of court noble, laying the groundwork for the future prominence of the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|ja|土御門家 (安倍氏)|lt=Tsuchimikado family}}.
== Biography ==
Born in {{ill|Karyaku|en|Karyaku|qid=Q1327198|lt=Karyaku}} 2 ({{ill|1327|en|1327|qid=Q5792|lt=1327}}) as the son of {{ill|Abe Yasukichi|ja|安倍泰吉|qid=DELETED_QID}}, Ariyo distinguished himself early as a skilled practitioner of {{ill|Onmyōdō|en|Onmyōdō|qid=Q1340540|lt=Onmyōdō}}. At the time, various branches of the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏}} were competing to claim the title of "main lineage" of the Abe family. 
In {{ill|Kōei|en|Kōei|qid=Q980266|lt=Kōei}} 3 ({{ill|1344|en|1344|qid=Q6073|lt=1344}}), Ariyo assumed the position of {{ill|Ōi no Gon no Suke|ja|大炊権頭}}, marking the beginning of his administrative career. In {{ill|Zhengping|en|Zhengping|qid=Q11123413|lt=Shōhei}} 9/{{ill|Bunna|en|Bunna|qid=Q1146252|lt=Bunwa}} 3 ({{ill|1354|en|1354|qid=Q6118|lt=1354}}), he supervised the ancient {{ill|Kishimai|ja|吉志舞}} ritual during the {{ill|Daijosai|en|Daijosai|qid=Q11433653|lt=Daijōsai}} of Emperor Go-Kōgon. Despite opposition from rival Abe clans, Ariyo's skill established him as a leading figure in Onmyōdō.
In {{ill|Bunna|en|Bunna|qid=Q1146252|lt=Bunwa}} 4 ({{ill|1355|en|1355|qid=Q6123|lt=1355}}), Ariyo was appointed {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽頭|lt=Onmyō no kami}} but resigned three years later due to intra-clan conflicts. He continued to serve in other roles, including {{ill|Right Capital Ward Officer|ja|左京大夫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakyō no Daibu|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakyō no Daibu|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=京職|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=京職|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=京職|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11374719}}, honing his expertise in astrology and divination.
In {{ill|Tianshou|en|Tianshou|qid=Q10939676|lt=Tenju}} 4/{{ill|Eiwa|ja|永和|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiwa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11131293}} 4 ({{ill|1378|en|1378|qid=Q6306|lt=1378}}), Ariyo gained the favor of {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|en|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|qid=Q248381|lt=Ashikaga Yoshimitsu}}, the third {{ill|Shogun|en|Shogun|qid=Q131767|lt=shōgun}} of the {{ill|Ashikaga shogunate|ja|Ashikaga Shogunate|2=ja|3=室町幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi shogunate|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1154406}}, after a successful prayer ritual. Yoshimitsu entrusted him with various spiritual and political responsibilities, elevating Ariyo's influence within both the imperial court and the shogunate.
In {{ill|Kakēi (Japan)|ja|嘉慶|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakei|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11419403}} 1 ({{ill|1387|en|1387|qid=Q6359|lt=1387}}), Ariyo was promoted to {{ill|Shōsanmi|ja|正三位}} and {{ill|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|ja|刑部卿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gyōbu-kyō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gyōbu-kyō|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=刑部省|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=刑部省|ja_comment=former now fixed redirect|3=刑部省|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6867320}}. By {{ill|Ōei|en|Ōei|qid=Q1193078|lt=Ōei}} 6 ({{ill|1399|en|1399|qid=Q6422|lt=1399}}), he had risen to {{ill|Juni|ja|従二位}}, the highest Rank ever achieved by an Onmyōji.
Ariyo passed away on {{ill|Ōei|en|Ōei|qid=Q1193078|lt=Ōei}} 12, {{ill|January 29|en|January 29|qid=Q2286|lt=January 29 (old calendar)}} ({{ill|1405|en|1405|qid=Q6124|lt=1405}} {{ill|February 28|en|February 28|qid=Q2362|lt=February 28}}), at the age of 79. His legacy as a master of Onmyōdō endured, with his name becoming synonymous with excellence in the field.
